19zxa.description: Leads special tactics teams of combat controllers, pararescuemen and other operators on special operations missions.

19zxb.title: Tactical Air Control Party (TACP) Officer
19zxb.description: Leads TACP teams that plan and control air support for Army and joint ground forces.

19zxc.title: Combat Rescue Officer
19zxc.description: Leads pararescue teams and plans personnel recovery missions to bring isolated people home.

1t0x1.title: Survival, Evasion, Resistance and Escape (SERE)
1t0x1.description: Teaches aircrew and high-risk personnel how to survive in the wild, evade capture and resist if taken prisoner.
1t0x1.training: Begins with a 15-day orientation course at JBSA-Lackland (Chapman Annex), TX, followed by extended SERE specialist training

1z1x1.title: Pararescue
1z1x1.description: Special warfare rescue specialists and paramedics who parachute, dive or climb into hostile or remote areas to treat and recover isolated personnel.
1z1x1.training: Pipeline of roughly two years after BMT, including selection at JBSA-Lackland, TX, combat dive, airborne, free-fall, SERE, a 39-week paramedic program and a 22-week apprentice course at Kirtland AFB, NM

1z2x1.title: Combat Control
1z2x1.description: Special operators who are also certified air traffic controllers, setting up assault zones and directing aircraft and airstrikes deep in hostile territory.
1z2x1.training: Long pipeline after BMT, including selection at JBSA-Lackland, TX, airborne, free-fall, SERE, 9 weeks of air traffic control and a 13-week apprentice course at Pope Army Airfield, NC

1z3x1.title: Tactical Air Control Party (TACP)
1z3x1.description: Embeds with Army and special operations ground units to call in and control air strikes close to friendly troops.
1z3x1.training: After BMT: Special Warfare Candidate Course and a 21-week TACP apprentice course at JBSA-Lackland, TX, then airborne, SERE and initial certification at Camp Bullis, TX and Nellis AFB, NV

1z4x1.title: Special Reconnaissance
1z4x1.description: Special operators who gather ground intelligence and environmental data and use tools like small drones to shape missions behind enemy lines.
1z4x1.training: Long pipeline after BMT, including selection at JBSA-Lackland, TX, pre-dive, airborne, military free-fall and SERE training

3e8x1.title: Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD)
3e8x1.description: Finds, disarms and safely disposes of bombs, improvised explosive devices and unexploded ordnance at home and in combat.
3e8x1.training: 26-day EOD preliminary course at Sheppard AFB, TX, then 143 days at the Naval School EOD at Eglin AFB, FL

63a.title: Acquisition Manager
63a.description: Manages programs that buy, build and field new space systems, keeping cost, schedule and performance on track.
63a.training: Commissioning (OTS, USAFA or ROTC); Space Force acquisition officers attend an acquisition initial qualification course.

17s.title: Cyberspace Effects Operations Officer
17s.description: Commands crews that run cyberspace weapon systems and satellite communications, from mission planning through execution, to protect Space Force networks and missions.
17s.training: Commissioning (OTS, USAFA or ROTC), then Undergraduate Cyberspace Training and mission qualification training.

5c0x1.title: Cyber Operations
5c0x1.description: Secures and defends Space Force networks, computer systems, and satellite and radio links. Guardians specialize in one of four tracks: defensive cyber (D), network operations (N), RF/SATCOM operations (R), or systems operations (S).
5c0x1.training: Basic Military Training, then several months of specialty-dependent technical training at Keesler AFB, MS (defensive cyber may instead use the USSF Cyber Combat Course).

62e3a.title: Aeronautical Engineer
62e3a.description: Developmental engineer who applies aeronautical engineering to design, test and improve systems for Space Force missions.
62e3a.training: Engineering bachelor's degree; commissioning through OTS, USAFA or ROTC.

62e3b.title: Astronautical Engineer
62e3b.description: Developmental engineer focused on spacecraft and space systems, planning and running engineering projects from design through testing.
62e3b.training: Engineering bachelor's degree; commissioning through OTS, USAFA or ROTC.

62e3c.title: Computer Systems Engineer
62e3c.description: Developmental engineer who designs and integrates the computer hardware and software inside Space Force systems.
62e3c.training: Engineering bachelor's degree; commissioning through OTS, USAFA or ROTC.

62e3e.title: Electrical/Electronic Engineer
62e3e.description: Developmental engineer who works on the electrical and electronic side of space and ground systems, such as power, sensors and communications.
62e3e.training: Engineering bachelor's degree; commissioning through OTS, USAFA or ROTC.

62e3h.title: Mechanical Engineer
62e3h.description: Developmental engineer who handles the physical structures, mechanisms and thermal design of Space Force systems.
62e3h.training: Engineering bachelor's degree; commissioning through OTS, USAFA or ROTC.

62e3i.title: Human Factors Engineer / Human Systems Integration
62e3i.description: Developmental engineer who makes sure systems are designed around the people who operate them, improving safety and usability.
62e3i.training: Engineering bachelor's degree; commissioning through OTS, USAFA or ROTC.

14n.title: Intelligence Officer
14n.description: Leads intelligence teams and turns collected information into assessments that support space and joint operations.
14n.training: Commissioning (OTS, USAFA or ROTC), then the Intelligence Officer Initial Skills course.

5i0x1.title: All Source Analyst
5i0x1.description: Combines intelligence from many sources (signals, imagery, human, open-source and more) into reports and briefings that support Space Force operations, testing and acquisitions.
5i0x1.training: Basic Military Training, then the All Source Intelligence Apprentice Course at Goodfellow AFB, TX.

5i0x1-sei-060.title: Geospatial Intelligence Analyst
5i0x1-sei-060.description: Studies satellite and other overhead imagery, along with map data, to spot unusual activity and possible threats. This is a training track inside the All Source Analyst specialty.
5i0x1-sei-060.training: Basic Military Training, then imagery/GEOINT training at Goodfellow AFB, TX, followed by Space Warfighter ISR formal training at Peterson SFB, CO.

5i0x1-sei-1s8.title: Targeting Analyst
5i0x1-sei-1s8.description: Builds and checks target intelligence, manages target lists, and assesses vulnerabilities and battle damage so commanders can plan precise effects. This is a training track inside the All Source Analyst specialty.
5i0x1-sei-1s8.training: Basic Military Training, then a multi-course targeting pipeline (Targeting Analyst, Target Coordinate Mensuration, Collateral Damage Estimation) at Goodfellow AFB, TX, followed by Space Warfighter ISR training at Peterson SFB, CO.

5i2x1.title: Cryptologic Analyst
5i2x1.description: Analyzes signals intelligence and cyber-network activity to find and report threats. Supports both SIGINT production and cryptologic support to cyberspace operations.
5i2x1.training: Basic Military Training, then technical training at Goodfellow AFB, TX.

5i2x1-signals-intelligence-analyst.title: Signals Intelligence Analyst
5i2x1-signals-intelligence-analyst.description: Collects and studies foreign electronic emissions and communications, then reports what they reveal so commanders can react quickly. Requires a polygraph and a top-level security clearance.
5i2x1-signals-intelligence-analyst.training: Basic Military Training, then about 5 months at Goodfellow AFB, TX, followed by Space Warfighter ISR training at Peterson SFB, CO.

13a.title: Astronaut
13a.description: Flies or crews human spaceflight missions, such as aboard the International Space Station, and advises on crewed spaceflight. A tiny, highly selective field rather than an entry-level job.

13s.title: Space Operations Officer
13s.description: Leads crews that operate space systems, and plans, directs and assesses space operations. Specializes in orbital warfare, space electronic warfare, space battle management, or space access and sustainment.
13s.training: Commissioning (OTS, USAFA or ROTC), then Undergraduate Space Training (UST) plus initial and mission qualification training for the chosen track.

5s0x1.title: Space Systems Operations
5s0x1.description: Runs the ground systems that track satellites, warn of missile launches, and support rocket launches and on-orbit operations. These Guardians keep space capabilities working and help defend them.
5s0x1.training: Basic Military Training, then Enlisted Undergraduate Space Training (EUST) at Vandenberg SFB, CA.

aeronautical-engineering.title: Aeronautical Engineering
aeronautical-engineering.description: Pilots who also manage aircraft and avionics engineering, structures and maintenance programs after graduate school.
aeronautical-engineering.training: Earned later in an aviation career through a funded master's degree program.

aviation-pilot.title: Aviation (Pilot)
aviation-pilot.description: Pilots who fly Coast Guard helicopters and airplanes for search and rescue, law enforcement and other missions.
aviation-pilot.training: About two years of Naval Flight School (Pensacola, FL / Corpus Christi, TX), then airframe training at Aviation Training Center Mobile, AL. Prior military pilots can use Direct Commission Aviation.

aet.title: Avionics Electrical Technician
aet.description: Maintains and troubleshoots the electronics on Coast Guard aircraft, including radar, radios, navigation and electrical systems.
aet.training: About 24 weeks of 'A' School at the Aviation Technical Training Center, Elizabeth City, NC, blended with on-the-job training at an air station.

amt.title: Aviation Maintenance Technician
amt.description: Keeps Coast Guard aircraft flying by inspecting and repairing engines, propellers, airframes and hydraulic systems. AMTs often fly as aircrew too.
amt.training: About 20 weeks of 'A' School at the Aviation Technical Training Center, Elizabeth City, NC, blended with on-the-job training at an air station.

ast.title: Aviation Survival Technician
ast.description: The Coast Guard's helicopter rescue swimmers. They deploy from helicopters to pull people out of the water, give emergency medical care, and maintain survival gear.
ast.training: 22-week rating course: EMT certification, rescue swimmer school, and aviation life-support equipment training.

avi.title: Aviation Engineering
avi.description: Supervises aircraft maintenance and aviation engineering programs at air stations and depots.
avi.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

cmm.title: Cyber Mission Management
cmm.description: Leads and technically guides Coast Guard cyber teams and operations.
cmm.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

cms.title: Cyber Mission Specialist
cms.description: A newer rating that defends Coast Guard and maritime-industry networks against hackers and other cyber threats.
cms.training: Navy Joint Cyber Analysis Course (JCAC), about 27 weeks, in Pensacola, FL.

ism.title: Information Systems Management
ism.description: Manages networks, computer systems and IT support for units and regions.
ism.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

it.title: Information Systems Technician
it.description: System administrators who keep computers, networks, servers and phone systems running for every mission.

bm.title: Boatswain's Mate
bm.description: Experts in seamanship and navigation who drive boats, handle lines and anchors, and often command small boats and units.

bosn.title: Boatswain
bosn.description: Senior seamanship expert who often commands small units and boats or runs deck operations on cutters.
bosn.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

gm.title: Gunner's Mate
gm.description: Maintains and repairs Coast Guard weapons, from handguns to large deck-mounted guns, and trains crews to use them safely.

weps.title: Weapons
weps.description: Manages weapons systems, armories and ordnance safety on cutters and at shore units.
weps.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

dc.title: Damage Controlman
dc.description: Handles welding, plumbing and carpentry, and leads firefighting and flood control so a damaged ship can keep going.

div.title: Diving
div.description: Supervises Coast Guard diving operations and dive lockers.
div.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

dv.title: Diver
dv.description: Works underwater on searches, recoveries, investigations, inspections and repairs. Only open to members who already reached E-4 in another rating.
dv.training: 21-week course at the Navy Diving and Salvage Training Center, Panama City, FL.

elc.title: Electronics
elc.description: Manages the installation and upkeep of electronics and C5ISR systems.
elc.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

em.title: Electrician's Mate
em.description: Installs and repairs electrical equipment, generators and machinery control systems at shore units and on cutters.

eng.title: Naval Engineering
eng.description: Leads the engineering department on cutters, keeping propulsion and ship systems running.
eng.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

et.title: Electronics Technician
et.description: Installs and fixes electronics such as radar, radios, navigation and C5ISR systems.

mat.title: Material Maintenance
mat.description: Runs maintenance and repair of shore facilities, boats and equipment.
mat.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

mk.title: Machinery Technician
mk.description: Maintains and repairs engines, hydraulics, refrigeration and other machinery on boats, cutters and shore units.

civil-engineering.title: Civil Engineering
civil-engineering.description: Engineers who plan, design, build and maintain the Coast Guard's shore buildings and infrastructure.
civil-engineering.training: Commission through OCS, the Academy, or Direct Commission Engineer.

cyberspace.title: Cyberspace
cyberspace.description: Officers who build, run, secure and defend Coast Guard networks and cyberspace systems.
cyberspace.training: Commission through OCS, the Academy, or a direct commission program; STEM degree helpful.

naval-engineering.title: Naval Engineering
naval-engineering.description: Engineers who design, build, maintain and sustain cutters and boats, often serving as a cutter's engineer officer.
naval-engineering.training: Commission through OCS, the Academy, or Direct Commission Engineer; a STEM degree helps.

dentist.title: Dentist
dentist.description: Dentists who provide dental care to Coast Guard members, mostly through the U.S. Public Health Service.
dentist.training: Licensed dentist; USPHS detail or direct employment.

environmental-health-officer.title: Environmental Health Officer
environmental-health-officer.description: Protects crews from disease, hazards and unsafe food or workplaces, and helps during disasters; mostly U.S. Public Health Service officers.

medical-administration.title: Medical Administration
medical-administration.description: Coast Guard officers who run clinics, manage health budgets and supervise Health Services Technicians.
medical-administration.training: Commission through OCS, then compete for graduate education in health administration.

nurse.title: Nurse
nurse.description: Nurse case managers who coordinate care across clinics to get members back to full duty, through direct employment or the U.S. Public Health Service.
nurse.training: Licensed nurse; USPHS detail or direct employment.

pharmacist.title: Pharmacist
pharmacist.description: Pharmacists who work in Coast Guard clinics and support public health emergencies, mostly through the U.S. Public Health Service.
pharmacist.training: Licensed pharmacist; USPHS detail or direct employment.

physician-physician-assistant.title: Physician / Physician Assistant
physician-physician-assistant.description: Doctors and PAs who care for Coast Guard members at clinics and in the field, some as flight surgeons. Many are U.S. Public Health Service officers detailed to the Coast Guard.
physician-physician-assistant.training: Direct Commission Physician Assistant / Health Services programs, the Interservice PA Program, or USPHS assignment.

psychologist-social-worker.title: Psychologist / Social Worker
psychologist-social-worker.description: Mental-health professionals who assess and treat members and help decide fitness for duty, largely through the U.S. Public Health Service.
psychologist-social-worker.training: Licensed provider; USPHS detail or direct employment.

is.title: Intelligence Specialist
is.description: Collects and analyzes information and turns it into intelligence briefings that help operations succeed.

iss.title: Intelligence Systems Specialist
iss.description: Leads intelligence operations and manages intelligence systems and security programs.
iss.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

inv.title: Criminal Investigator
inv.description: Special agent with the Coast Guard Investigative Service who conducts criminal investigations.
inv.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

iv.title: Investigator
iv.description: A Reserve-only rating of enlisted criminal investigators who work with the Coast Guard Investigative Service (CGIS).

me.title: Maritime Enforcement Specialist
me.description: The Coast Guard's law enforcement and security specialists. They lead boardings, protect ports, and train crews in tactics and use of force.

mles.title: Maritime Law Enforcement and Security Specialist
mles.description: Senior law enforcement expert who leads tactical teams, training and port security work.
mles.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

prevention-marine-safety.title: Prevention (Marine Safety)
prevention-marine-safety.description: Officers who inspect ships, investigate marine accidents, manage waterways and enforce port safety and security rules to stop disasters before they happen.
prevention-marine-safety.training: Commission through OCS, the Academy, or the Maritime Academy Direct Commission program.

mssd.title: Maritime Safety Specialist Deck
mssd.description: Inspects commercial vessels for deck and safety compliance and helps investigate marine accidents.
mssd.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

msse.title: Maritime Safety Specialist Engineering
msse.description: Inspects the engineering plants of commercial vessels for safety and compliance.
msse.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

mssr.title: Maritime Safety Specialist Response
mssr.description: Leads pollution and hazardous-material response and related port operations.
mssr.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

mst.title: Marine Science Technician
mst.description: Inspects ships and waterfront facilities for safety and responds to oil and chemical spills.

hs.title: Health Services Technician
hs.description: The Coast Guard's medics. They give emergency and routine medical care to crews and help run clinics and sick bays.

med.title: Medical Administration
med.description: Manages clinic administration, budgets and medical readiness programs.
med.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

afloat-cutterman.title: Afloat (Cutterman)
afloat-cutterman.description: Officers who drive and lead crews on Coast Guard cutters, from law-enforcement 'white hulls' to buoy tenders and polar icebreakers.
afloat-cutterman.training: Commission through OCS or the Coast Guard Academy, then cutter assignments.

response.title: Response
response.description: Officers who run shore-based operations: command center search and rescue, boat forces, law enforcement, deployable specialized forces, spill response and emergency management.
response.training: Commission through OCS or the Coast Guard Academy, then response assignments.

os.title: Operations Specialist
os.description: Runs communications and coordination around the clock in command centers and on cutters, including planning search and rescue cases.

oss.title: Operations Systems Specialist
oss.description: Manages command center operations, communications and operational systems.
oss.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

rmm.title: Robotics Mission Manager
rmm.description: New CWO specialty (2026) serving as the Coast Guard's top operational and technical authority on robots, drones and autonomous systems.
rmm.training: Normal path is from the RMS rating; selection criteria still being announced.

rms.title: Robotics Mission Specialist
rms.description: The newest rating (announced June 2026). Operates and maintains drones and other unmanned systems in the air, on the surface and underwater, including counter-drone work.
rms.training: No 'A' School announced yet; first members come in by lateral transfer, and future accessions start at E-4.

financial-management.title: Financial Management
financial-management.description: Officers who handle budgets, accounting, audits and supply for Coast Guard units.
financial-management.training: Commission through OCS or the Academy; advanced degree (e.g. MBA) helpful.

intelligence.title: Intelligence
intelligence.description: Officers who collect, analyze and share intelligence, with assignments in counterintelligence, cryptology, cyber and investigations.
intelligence.training: Commission through OCS, the Academy, or Direct Commission Intelligence Officer (DCIO).

law-judge-advocate-cgjag.title: Law (Judge Advocate / CGJAG)
law-judge-advocate-cgjag.description: Coast Guard lawyers who give legal advice on operations, military justice and every other part of the service.
law-judge-advocate-cgjag.training: Law degree and bar admission required; enter via Direct Commission Lawyer or later through funded law school.

reserve-component-manager.title: Reserve Component Manager
reserve-component-manager.description: Officers who organize, recruit, train and manage the Coast Guard Reserve force.

cs.title: Culinary Specialist
cs.description: Plans and cooks meals for crews ashore and at sea, and handles the food budget, ordering and storage.

f-s.title: Finance and Supply
f-s.description: Oversees budgets, purchasing, contracting and supply for units.
f-s.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

inf.title: Public Information
inf.description: Leads public affairs work and media relations for commands.
inf.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

mu.title: Musician
mu.description: Professional musicians in the U.S. Coast Guard Band. Players win the job by audition and enlist directly as E-6; it is not open to regular recruits.
mu.training: No 'A' School; selected by competitive audition in New London, CT.

pa.title: Public Affairs Specialist
pa.description: Tells the Coast Guard's story through writing, photography, video and media relations.
pa.training: 26-week course at the Defense Information School, Fort Meade, MD.

pers.title: Personnel Administration
pers.description: Runs personnel and administrative offices handling pay, records and HR policy.
pers.training: Selected from senior enlisted (usually E-6 and up) by a CWO appointment board; appointed as CWO2.

sk.title: Storekeeper
sk.description: Handles logistics: buying supplies, managing inventory and contracts, and tracking money.

ta.title: Talent Acquisition Specialist
ta.description: A recruiting rating created so recruiting can be a full career instead of a one-tour assignment. Open to members at E-5 and above, phased in starting in 2025.

yn.title: Yeoman
yn.description: The Coast Guard's personnel and HR experts, handling pay, travel, records and transfers.
